name: Act of March 3, 1871 providing for the removal of Kickapoo and other tribes roving on the Mexico and Texas borders to reservations in Indian Territory
aka: Indian appropriation act of March 3, 1871, Kickapoo clause
landTaken: The Commission found the Oklahoma reservation contained 206,466 acres, of which about 184,300 were ceded in 1891 and the rest mostly allotted to tribal members (Docket 318).
compensation: The Commission found the 1891 agreement paid $64,650.00 in cash, and that in 1908 Congress, on the Kickapoo's petition, appropriated $215,000 more, a total of $279,650. The Docket 318 compromise added $273,250; the tribe's general council approved it 38 to 7 on August 3, 1968.
today: The Commission found the Kickapoo received title to the reservation as of October 1, 1874 as a gratuity from the United States. The Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma's general council met at the Kickapoo Community Center in McLoud, Oklahoma, to approve the 1968 settlement.
promises: No treaty. Congress appropriated up to $40,000 for the removal of the Kickapoo and other tribes roving on the borders of Mexico and Texas to reservations within the Indian Territory, and for their settlement and subsistence there.
The reservation where they were settled (Royce Area 650) was set apart later by the President, according to Royce, in 1883.

breaches.what: The Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma claimed before the Indian Claims Commission that the price paid for about 184,300 acres of its Oklahoma reservation (Royce Area 650), ceded by the agreement of September 9, 1891, was unconscionable. The claim was settled by compromise for $273,250.

openQuestions: treaties.json: this entry and cession-1870-07-15-kickapoo are two appropriation acts, not cessions, and both point to Royce 650, the reservation later set apart for the Mexican Kickapoo and ceded in 1891.
The settlement is counted as litigation only. Whether the 1891 agreement was obtained improperly, which the 1908 appropriation may reflect, was not found in a government or court source opened.
No Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma or Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas account was opened.

plain.promised: No treaty. In 1871 Congress paid to move Kickapoo and others living on the Mexico and Texas borders to reservations in Indian Territory and support them there.
plain.happened: No court or Commission finding of a breach. The Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma claimed that the 1891 price for most of its later reservation was unconscionable, and the claim was settled.
plain.today: The Indian Claims Commission approved a $273,250 compromise in 1969, after Congress had added $215,000 to the 1891 price in 1908.
